en: In terms of geography.

To dress or decorate in a hip fashion.

ex.ja: 都会には、流行に敏感な人や、パーティー好きの人がたくさんいます。

en: A female host.
A female innkeeper.

ex.ja: 彼はエアホステスと結婚した。

ex.en: The hostess couldn't possibly put up with his arrogance.

ex.en: Let's drink to our charming hostess!
ex.ja: 魅力的なホステスのために乾杯！

note.ja: host（もてなす人）+ -ess（女性形）。「女主人」。

note.ja: 「荒れ野」は古英語 mōr。「係留する」は中世オランダ語 maren（つなぐ）からで別語。

en: A type of flattish bun, usually cut in two horizontally, toasted and spread with butter, etc., before being eaten.
A cupcake-shaped baked good (for example of cornbread, banana bread, or a chocolate dough), sometimes glazed but typically without frosti…
To eat muffins.
To feed muffins to.

muffin.ety: From earlier moofin, probably a diminutive of Low German Muffe ("small cake"; Muffen (plural)), from Middle Low German muffe (“small pastry”). An alternative, and phonologically less plausible theory suggests a connection to Old French (pain) moflet (“roll”, literally “soft (bread)”). Sense “vulva” influenced by muff.

ex.en: You are eating a muffin for breakfast.
ex.ja: あなたは朝食にマフィンを食べている。

ex.en: I don't know why I need to stop eating muffins.
ex.ja: どうしてマフィンを食べるの止めなくちゃいけないのか、それが分かんないんだ。

ex.en: How many blueberry muffins did you eat yesterday?
ex.ja: ブルーベリーマフィン、昨日幾つ食べたの？

note.ja: 語源ははっきりしない。低地ドイツ語 muffe（小さなケーキ）とされる。

en: A sash worn with a kimono.
A strip of paper looped around a book or other product.

ex.en: Her kimono and obi combination is smart, isn't it?
ex.ja: 彼女の着物と帯の取り合わせはおつだね。

note.ja: 日本語「帯」から。

en: Covered with or containing oil.

ex.ja: 男性の方が女性より肌が脂っぽいって本当ですか？

ex.en: My clothes have an oily smell because I ate at an okonomiyaki place.
ex.ja: お好み焼き屋に行ったので、なんか服が油臭い！

note.ja: out（外へ）+ spoken（話された）。「遠慮なく話す」。

en: A part associated with the mouth of certain invertebrates, somewhat analogous to the palate of vertebrates.
A projection in the throat of certain bilabiate flowers as the snapdragon.

ex.ja: 彼はワインの味がよく分かる。

ex.en: Their grapes suit my palate.
ex.ja: このブドウは私の好みに合う。

ex.en: Foreign rice is hard and tasteless, and doesn't appeal to the Japanese palate.
ex.ja: 外米はぼそぼそしていて、日本人の口には合わない。

note.ja: ラテン語 palatum（口蓋）から。「口蓋」→ 味を感じる所 →「味覚」。palatable（おいしい）。

en: The base or foot of a column, statue, vase, lamp.
A place of reverence or honor.
To set or support on (or as if on) a pedestal.

pedestal.ety: Borrowed from Middle French piédestal, itself borrowed from Italian piedistallo (literally “foot stand”). Spelling influenced by Latin pēs, pedem.

ex.en: He has her on a pedestal.
ex.ja: 彼は彼女をあがめたてています。

en: A chart, list, or record of ancestors, to show breeding, especially distinguished breeding.
A person's ancestral history; ancestry, lineage.
Having a pedigree.
Purebred.
To determine the pedigree of (an animal).

pedigree.ety: From Anglo-Norman pé de grue, a variant of Old French pié de gru (“foot of a crane”), from Latin pes (“foot”) + grus (“crane”).

note.ja: 古フランス語 pié de grue（ツルの足）から。家系図の枝分かれの線がツルの足に似ていたことから。

en: Fraudulent; fake; having a misleading appearance.
A person who assumes an identity or quality other than their own.
A person who professes beliefs or opinions that they do not hold.
To fake.

phony.ety: Of unknown origin. Perhaps an alteration of fawny (“gilt brass ring used by swindlers”) (1781), from Irish fáinne (“ring”).

ex.en: I got sucked in on a lot of phony deals.
ex.ja: 何回もいかさまにだまされましたよ。

ex.en: My mother says that the child's illnesses are phony.
ex.ja: その子の病気はいつも仮病であると母親は言っている。

ex.en: Japan disproved phony accusations of computer chip dumping.
ex.ja: コンピューターチップのダンピングに関する不当な非難に日本は反論しました。

note.ja: fawney（にせの金の指輪）から変化した語とされる。「にせの」。

en: The point of a pin.
Something infinitesimal; a tiny point.
Extremely precise or specific, especially regarding location.
To identify or locate (someone or something) precisely or with great accuracy.
Any of various respiratory diseases in birds, especially infectious coryza.
To remove the pips from.

pip.ety: From Middle English pippe, from Middle Dutch pip, from post-classical Latin pipita, from Latin pītuīta (“mucus, phlegm, head cold”). Doublet of pituita.

ex.en: Now stop asking questions, Pip. I'm busy.
ex.ja: さて、質問はおわりだ。ピップ君、わたしは忙しいのだ。

ex.en: "I want to be a farmer," said Pip.
ex.ja: 農園主になりたいなあ。とピップが言いました。

ex.en: "What shall we do with the rubbish, Mr Wood?" asked Pip.
ex.ja: そのガラクタはどうしたらいいのですか。ウッドさん。とピップが尋ねました。

note.ja: pippin（種から育てたリンゴ）の短縮。「（果物の）種」。

en: In a pleasant manner; so as to achieve a pleasant result.
Lightly.

pleasantly.ety: From Middle English pleasauntly; equivalent to pleasant + -ly.

ex.en: I was pleasantly surprised by the low price.
ex.ja: 値段が安いのはうれしい驚きだった。

ex.en: I was pleasantly surprised by the low prices.
ex.ja: 値段が安いのはうれしい驚きだった。

ex.en: He spoke to me pleasantly.
ex.ja: 彼は愛想よく話し掛けてきた。

en: To wonder, think of deeply.
To consider (something) carefully and thoroughly.
A period of deep thought.

ponder.ety: From Middle English ponderen, from Old French ponderer (“to weigh, balance, ponder”) from Latin ponderāre (“to weigh, ponder”), from pondus (“weight”), from pendere (“to weigh”); see pendent and pound.

ex.en: We all pondered over what had taken place.
ex.ja: 我々は皆、起こったことについて深く考えた。

ex.en: She pondered the question for a while.
ex.ja: 彼女はしばらくの間その問題を熟考した。

ex.en: Tom pondered his next move.
ex.ja: トムは次なる行動をじっくり考えた。

note.ja: ラテン語 ponderare（量る）から。pond（重さ）+ er。重さを量るようにじっくり考える →「熟考する」。pendere（量る）の仲間。

en: Skillfulness or extraordinary ability in a particular area of expertise; dexterity, mastery, or proficiency.
Distinguished bravery or courage, especially in battle; heroism.

prowess.ety: From Middle English prowesse, prouwesse, proues, prouesce, prouesse (“bravery in battle; act of bravery; excellence; nobility of character; intelligence”), from Old French proeche, proesce, proeësche (“goodness; excellence; bravery”), from Old French preu, prou, prouz, proz, pruz (“good; excellent; brave”). Compare English proud.

note.ja: 古フランス語 proesse（勇敢さ）から。prou（勇敢な）。proud と同系。「腕前・武勇」。

A type of instant noodles.
amen

To scare, startle, unsettle, or unnerve.
Any of various plants of the genera Rhinanthus and Pedicularis, whose seeds produce a rattling noise in the wind.
A baby’s toy designed to make sound when shaken, usually containing loose grains or pellets in a hollow container.

rattle.ety: From Middle English ratelen, of uncertain origin; perhaps borrowed from Middle Dutch ratelen or of native origin related to Old English hratele, hrætele (“a plant known for its rustling or rattling sound”), ultimately imitative. The noun (c. 1500) is from the verb.

ex.en: The wind is strong, and the house is rattling.
ex.ja: 風が強くて家がガタガタ鳴ってる。

ex.en: The wind was so strong that the windows rattled.
ex.ja: 風がとても強かったので、窓ががたがた音をたてた。

ex.en: She got rattled by the stupid question.
ex.ja: 彼女は馬鹿らしい質問をされていらいらした。

note.ja: 中世オランダ語 ratelen（ガラガラ鳴る）から。擬音語。「ガタガタ鳴る」→「動揺させる」、赤ちゃんの「ガラガラ」。rattlesnake（ガラガラヘビ）。

ex.ja: 私たちは新聞の再生利用を始めました。

ex.ja: 黙っていたことを後悔した人より、しゃべったことを後悔した人が多い。

ex.ja: 今更悔やんでも後の祭りだ。

en: A clear, slightly alkaline liquid secreted into the mouth by the salivary glands and mucous glands, consisting of water, mucin, protein, …

saliva.ety:

Displaced Middle English slaver, slavere ("saliva"; whence Modern English slaver); and Middle English spyttle, spetel, spatel, spotel ("saliva"; whence Modern English spittle, spettle, spattle).

en: The ordinal form of the number seventeen.
One of seventeen equal parts of a whole.
An interval of two octaves and a third.

ex.en: Yesterday was my seventeenth birthday.

ex.ja: 学校への近道だよ。

ex.en: I know a shortcut. Follow me.
ex.ja: 近道、知ってるよ。ついておいで。

note.ja: short（短い）+ cut（切り通し）。「近道」→ 操作の「ショートカット」。

en: An adherent of Sikhism.
Of, or relating to the Sikhs or to Sikhism.

note.ja: パンジャーブ語 sikh（弟子）から。サンスクリット語 śiṣya（弟子）。「シク教徒」。

en: To kill; to murder.
To eradicate or stamp out.
That slays (in any sense).
Something excellent, amazing, or fashionable.
Used to express approval or amazement.

slay.ety:

note.ja: 古英語 slēan（打つ・殺す）から。slaughter と同じ。（俗）「圧倒する・最高にかっこいい」。

ex.ja: 離着陸の際にはシートベルトをしめて下さい。

ex.en: During takeoff, one's ears pop.
ex.ja: 離陸する時に、耳がキーンとなります。

en: That can be taxed.
Subject to taxation.
Something on which tax must be paid.
A piece of indoor sporting equipment used to allow for the motions of running or walking while staying in one place.
A mill worked by persons treading upon steps on the periphery of a wide wheel having a horizontal axis. It was used principally as a mean…
To exercise on a treadmill.
To keep busy, for example, with work or with other tasks, without being able to get ahead or make progress towards long-term goals.

treadmill.ety: From tread + mill. Its figurative senses refer to the idea that running on a treadmill requires continued effort and motion to remain in the same place.

ex.en: I broke a sweat running on the treadmill.
ex.ja: 私はトレッドミル上を走って汗をかいた。

note.ja: tread（踏む）+ mill（水車・粉ひき）。昔の囚人の踏み車 →「ルームランナー」→ 単調な繰り返しの仕事。

en: Impossible to avoid; bound to happen.
Not voidable; incapable of being made null or void.
Something that cannot be avoided.

unavoidable.ety: From Middle English unavoidable, equivalent to un- + avoidable.

ex.en: A sacrifice is unavoidable.
ex.ja: 犠牲はつきものさ。

ex.en: He had to part from her owing to unavoidable circumstances many years ago.
ex.ja: 彼は何年も前にやむを得ない事情のため、彼女と別れなければなりませんでした。

ex.en: Due to unavoidable circumstances this summer I can't stay in my holiday cottage.
ex.ja: よんどころない事情で、今年の夏は別荘で過ごせないんだ。

note.ja: un（否定）+ avoid（避ける）+ -able。「避けられない」。

en: Done by one side only.
Affecting only one side of the body.

unilateral.ety: A modern creation (circa 1802), from New Latin ūnilaterālis (“one-sided”), from Latin ūnus (“one”) + laterālis (“sided, lateral”), equivalent to uni- + lateral.

en: To fight for superiority; to contend; to compete eagerly so as to gain something.

vie.ety: Apheretic form of envy, from Middle English envien, from Old French envier, from Latin invītō.

ex.ja: 夏はスイカに限る！

en: Lying toward the west.
Moving or oriented toward the west.
Toward the west.
The western region or countries; the west.

westward.ety: From Middle English westward, from Old English westweard.

ex.ja: 太陽が西に傾いた。

en: To become wide or wider.
To make wide or wider.

Having a pH less than 7, or being sour, or having the strength to neutralize alkalis, or turning a litmus paper red.

en: An area of decayed vegetation (particularly sphagnum moss) which forms a wet spongy ground too soft for walking.

A man of French birth or nationality.

ex.ja: 私はカーペットよりも硬い木の床が好きです。

lofty.ety: From Middle English lofty, lofti, lofte (“of high rank; noble; ornate”), equivalent to loft (“sky, firmament; upper room”) + -y.

ex.ja: 彼の成功は長年の不屈の努力の結果だ。

ex.ja: 忍耐は成功にはとりわけ必要である。

ex.ja: 忍耐は、ご承知のように、成功への鍵です。

A device that lowers engine coolant temperature by conducting heat to the air, through metal fins.

Also Einsteinian relativity: the reliance of the nature of physical phenomena (such as gravity, light, mass, and time) on the relative mo…

relativity.ety:
From relative (“connected to or depending on something else”) + -ity (suffix forming nouns from adjectives where the nouns refer to the properties, qualities, or states described by the adjectives). Morphologically relative + -ity.

ex.en: Few scientists understand the theory of relativity.
ex.ja: 相対性理論を理解する科学者は少ない。

en: Respected or given reverence.
To criticize or disapprove of someone or something through scornful jocularity; to make fun of.
Derision; mocking or humiliating words or behavior.
An object of sport or laughter; a laughing stock.

ridicule.ety:
The obsolete adjective is borrowed from French ridicule, from Latin rīdiculus (“laughable, comical, amusing, absurd, ridiculous”), from ridere (“to laugh”).
The noun is either from French, noun use of adjective, or from Latin rīdiculum, noun use of neuter of rīdiculus.
The verb is from the noun or else from French ridiculer, from ridicule.

ex.en: It is not good to ridicule him in public.
ex.ja: 公衆の面前で彼を嘲笑するのはよくない。

ex.en: It is mean of you to ridicule him in public.
ex.ja: 人前で彼を冷やかすなんて君は意地悪だ。

ex.en: If you do that, you're going to subject yourself to ridicule.
ex.ja: そんなことをすれば笑いものの種なるよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 ridiculum（笑いもの）から。ridere（笑う）。「あざける」。ridiculous と同じ。

en: A member of an indigenous Finno-Ugric people of Lapland.
Relating to the Sami people of northern Scandinavia, or the Sami languages.

From Northern Sami Sápmi, from one of the Sami languages, of uncertain origin/meaning, but possibly related to Proto-Balto-Slavic *źémijāˀ (“land”). Displaced native Old English Finn (the direct descendant is Finn (“person from Finland”)). More at Sápmi and Sami.

ex.en: Sami drove the car at 160 miles an hour.
ex.ja: サミは時速160マイルで車を運転しました。

ex.en: Sami was standing at the bus stop.
ex.ja: サミはバス停留所で立っていた。

ex.en: Sami wants to eat some ice cream.
ex.ja: サミはアイスが食べたい。

note.ja: 北欧の先住民族の自称から。

en: A person who sculpts; an artist who produces sculpture.

sculptor.ety: Borrowed from Latin sculptor, equivalent to sculpt + -or.

ex.en: The sculptor carved wood into an image of Buddha.
ex.ja: その彫刻家は木で仏像を刻んだ。

ex.en: The sculptor belongs to the Renaissance school.
ex.ja: その彫刻家はルネサンス派に属する。

ex.en: The completion of the bronze statue did credit to the sculptor.
ex.ja: 銅像の完成はその彫刻家に名誉となった。

note.ja: ラテン語 sculpere（彫る）+ -tor。「彫刻家」。sculpture と同じ。

en: A playoff in the round with only four players or teams left, the stage before the final.
A competition that narrows a field of contestants (semifinalists) to a set of finalists, for a subsequent final.

semifinal.ety: From Latin semifinalis, equivalent to semi- + final.

ex.en: The team won the semifinals and advanced to the finals.
ex.ja: そのチームは準決勝に勝って決勝に進出した。

note.ja: semi（半分）+ final（決勝）。「準決勝」。

A thin layer of a substance (such as oil) spread on a solid or liquid surface.

ex.ja: 僕はこの上なく実直な男だ。

ex.ja: あれ？私たちって、もしかして誹謗中傷されてる？

ex.ja: デメトリウスは私を中傷しているよ！

note.ja: 古フランス語 esclandre（醜聞）から。ギリシャ語 skandalon（つまずきの石）。scandal と同じ語源。「（口頭の）中傷」。

ex.ja: 彼はとても世慣れているが、まだ非常に若い人です。

Borrowed from French adepte, from Latin adeptus (“who has achieved”), the past participle of adipisci (“to attain”).

ex.en: He is adept at telling lies.
ex.ja: 彼はうそつきの名人だ。

ex.en: He is adept in swimming.
ex.ja: 彼は水泳の達人だ。

ex.en: He is an adept climber.
ex.ja: 彼は熟練した登山家だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 adeptus（獲得した）から。ad + apisci（手に入れる）。「熟達した」。錬金術の奥義を得た人から。

en: Being of advantage, beneficial.

advantageous.ety: From advantage + -ous or from Middle French avantageus (French avantageux). See advantage.

ex.en: This marriage will be advantageous to his career.
ex.ja: この結婚は彼の将来にとって有利になるだろう。

ex.en: The general situation is advantageous to us.
ex.ja: 全般的な状況はわれわれに有利だ。

ex.en: The strong yen was advantageous to our company.
ex.ja: 円高は我が社にとって好都合であった。

note.ja: advantage（有利）+ -ous。「有利な」。

In, or found while in, a vessel at sea or on another body of water.

ex.ja: 船がやっと浮かんだ。

ex.en: The company managed to keep afloat.
ex.ja: 会社は何とか倒産せずにすんだ。

ex.en: There are strange rumors afloat.
ex.ja: 奇妙な噂がたっている。

en: The quality of being agile; the power of moving the limbs quickly and easily; quickness of motion
A faculty of being agile in body, mind, or figuratively.

agility.ety: From late Middle English, borrowed from Middle French agilité, from Latin agilitās, from agilis (“nimble, fleet, quick”), equivalent to agile + -ity.

note.ja: agile（機敏な）+ -ity。ラテン語 agere（動かす）。「機敏さ」。act と同じ。

A group of many islands.

en: Swollen with fluid or gas.
Excessively or extremely large or wealthy.

ex.en: The bloated profits of farmers at the time were something again.
ex.ja: 当時の農家の暴利はすさまじかった。

ex.en: My lower abdomen feels bloated.
ex.ja: 下腹部が張ります。

note.ja: bloat（膨らむ）+ -ed。北欧語 blautr（柔らかい）とされる。「膨れた・肥大化した」。

en: Of, or pertaining to, a dog or dogs.
Dog-like.
Any member of Caninae, the only living subfamily of Canidae.
Any of certain extant canids regarded as similar to the dog or wolf (including coyotes, jackals, etc.) but distinguished from the vulpine…

canine.ety: From Latin canīnus (“of dogs, doglike, dogtooth”), from canis (“dog”). Compare French canin.

ex.en: I snapped the thread on my canine.
ex.ja: プチッ、と糸を犬歯で噛み切った。

en: Of, relating to, or being a cause of something; causing.
A word (such as because) that expresses a reason or a cause.

causal.ety: Borrowed from Late Latin causalis, from Latin causa (“cause”), equivalent to cause + -al, see cause.

note.ja: cause（原因）+ -al。「因果関係の」。casual（偶然の・気軽な）と綴りが似ているので注意。

en: A person, usually a young, attractive female, who encourages applause and cheers at a sports event, and wearing a specially-designed unif…
A person who rallies support for any cause.

ex.ja: チアリーダーの選抜テストを受けたいのです。

ex.en: She can dance the best of all the cheerleaders.
ex.ja: 彼女はチアガールの中で最もじょうずに踊ることができる。

ex.en: Ann is a cheerleader.
ex.ja: アンはチアガールです。

note.ja: cheer（声援）+ leader（先導する人）。「チアリーダー」→「熱烈な支持者」。

en: A strong fortress that sits high above a city.
A stronghold or fortified place.

citadel.ety: From French citadelle, from Italian cittadella, diminutive of città (“city”), from Latin cīvitās.

note.ja: イタリア語 cittadella（小さな都市）から。città（都市）。「城砦」。city と同じ。
